subject: Investigate: trial credit cluster — disposable domains & shared IPs
messages:
From: fraudbot@monitoring.redwood.com
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 05 Jun 2026 09:12:01 +0000
Subject: Alert: cluster of trial credit grants (14) — disposable domains / shared IPs

Automated fraud alert:

Summary:
- 14 trial credit grants issued in the last 2 hours
- Common signals: 10 accounts using disposable-email domains (tmpmail/*), 9 from two /24s (shared cloud IPs), similar user-agent fingerprints
- Total credit cost: ~480k tokens (~$38 estimated)

Actions suggested:
1) Hold manual reversals for high-confidence duplicates (block by email domain + IP).
2) Run HubSpot & device-ID cross-check for customer records.
3) If >10 accounts confirmed bots, consider roll-back and mark these patterns in the sign-up pipeline to block future grants.

Attachments: flagged_signups_20260605.csv (CSV stub with: email, signup_ip, ua_hash, grant_id)
Link: https://grafana.redwood-inference.internal/d/txG3/signup-fraud-signals

--fraudbot
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: aditya_rao@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Cc: evelyn_hart@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 05 Jun 2026 09:40:13 +0000
Subject: Re: Alert: cluster of trial credit grants (14) — disposable domains / shared IPs

Thanks for the flag — I reviewed the CSV quickly. A few notes:
- Several entries share the same cookie/device fingerprint across different emails (strong duplicate signal).
- A handful look borderline (different UAs but same AWS subnet + disposable domain).

Proposal:
1) Immediate step: suspend credit balances for the 6 accounts with identical fingerprints and issue a temporary hold on new self-serve credits from the offending /24s.
2) For the remaining 8, assign to manual review (CS) and pause auto-issuance for 24 hours while we confirm.
3) If confirmed fraudulent, reverse the grants and add the patterns to the signup denylist.

Can you run HubSpot cross-checks and surface any paid conversions? Also tagging Evelyn for policy escalation if we need to deviate from the usual automated reversal window.

Thanks — Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Manager, Growth & PLG Ops
Redwood Inference
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Cc: evelyn_hart@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 05 Jun 2026 10:05:37 +0000
Subject: Re: Alert: cluster of trial credit grants (14) — disposable domains / shared IPs

Agree with Hannah's triage. Quick tasks I'm running now:
- HubSpot: pulling contact records for the 14 grants (HubSpot IDs attached in link).
- Device signal enrichment: will check IP WHOIS and see if any map to known proxy providers.
- Token snapshot: estimating real usage per account (to prioritize reversal impact).

If we have confirmation on 6 high-confidence duplicates, I support reversing credits immediately and sending a standard reversal notice. For the borderline group, we should hold credits and request small verification steps (e.g., company email or minimal KYC) before re-issuing.

Related: if FastFlow (their trial appears in the CSV) reaches out claiming it's a legitimate set of sandbox accounts, we should ask for proof of control (billing contact) before re-issuing credits.

Aditya
Principal Analyst, Growth Data
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Cc: evelyn_hart@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 05 Jun 2026 13:18:02 +0000
Subject: Re: Alert: cluster of trial credit grants (14) — disposable domains / shared IPs

Update after manual checks:
- Confirmed duplicates: 6 accounts share ua_hash X3A9 and the same cookie fingerprint; all 6 used disposable domains (example domains listed in CSV).
- Borderline: 5 accounts from same /24 but with different fingerprints; they have no HubSpot contact.
- Possible legitimate claim: 3 accounts list FastFlow billing emails (billing@fastflow.ai / support@fastflow.ai) — those have company domains but low signal of ownership (no HubSpot contact).

I recommend:
- Revoke credits for the 6 confirmed duplicates today and attach revoke_manifest_20260606.csv for finance to process.
- Hold the 5 borderline accounts for 48 hours pending response to verification email.
- Reach out to FastFlow billing to request verification of those 3 accounts before any reversal — if they claim legitimate use, escalate to policy to consider a manual exception.

Attaching: revoke_manifest_20260606.csv (stub)
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 06 Jun 2026 08:23:51 +0000
Subject: Decision: reverse confirmed duplicates; hold borderline; outreach to FastFlow

Thanks team — decision: execute Monica's recommendation.
Actions to run now:
- Ops: reverse the 6 confirmed duplicate credit grants and tag them as "fraud-revoked". Finance should be notified with revoke_manifest_20260606.csv.
- Product: add the offending /24 ranges to a temporary throttle rule for 72 hours and disable auto-grant for disposable-email domains.
- Growth/CS: send an outreach email to billing@fastflow.ai and support@fastflow.ai asking for proof of account ownership (reply within 48 hours). Do not re-issue credits until verification is received.
- Log: mark this incident for the monthly security_compliance digest and include the Grafana dashboard snapshot.

If any of the three FastFlow accounts can prove ownership, we will evaluate re-issuing credits on a case-by-case basis and document the reasoning.

Evelyn Hart
Head of Growth Ops
Redwood Inference
